title: Weekly Sales Totals Using DATE_TRUNC
description:
Aggregate daily sales into weekly totals using DATE_TRUNC to group by the start of each ISO week.

**Table: daily_sales** — `sale_date`, `amount`

Output columns: `week_start`, `total_sales`, `days_with_sales`. Order by `week_start`.
solution_sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('week', sale_date) AS week_start, SUM(amount) AS total_sales, COUNT(*) AS days_with_sales FROM daily_sales GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('week', sale_date) ORDER BY week_start

test_cases.description: 13 daily records spanning 4 weeks; 4 rows of weekly aggregates

hints: DATE_TRUNC('week', date) truncates a date to the Monday of its ISO week — all dates in the same week map to the same Monday.
Use the truncated date in both the SELECT and GROUP BY; you can use the alias in ORDER BY.
explanation: DATE_TRUNC('week', sale_date) maps each date to its week's Monday. Dates Jan 5-7 → week 2026-01-05 (3 days, 3150 total). Jan 12-15 → week 2026-01-12 (4 days, 4550). Jan 19-22 → week 2026-01-19 (4 days, 3870). Jan 26-27 → week 2026-01-26 (2 days, 2950). 13 daily rows collapse into 4 weekly rows.
